title: AI game art asset creation?
author: rapkannibale
selftext:
Has anyone found a tool or service where I could have AI create game assets (2D) with a consistent art style and that allows me to create assets with specific dimensions and transparency?

Thanks so much in advance!

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: I haven’t but I will check it out

comments.author: Lihinel
comments.body:
Not quite, but depending on the style you want, a long enough reusable style prompt and a few attachments of related assets, Gemini with Nano Banana Pro is pretty decent.

It'll likely get you about 75 to 90% of the way. For the rest I would suggest an image editing tool of yous choice. I use GIMP, most simple programs will do.

(Mainly for dimensions and transparency, but also to adjust lightness, saturation or hue if needed.)

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Once you know what you're doing without AI, it makes sense what to do with AI.

replies.body: Definitely interested in checking it out

comments.author: intLeon
comments.body: If you tinker a little you can train your own lora for z image turbo model. It takes 12gb vram for training and less than 8 for running. You can then build a workflow to generate transparent sprites but its a little advanced.

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: I definitely have good enough hardware to do this and am somewhat familiar with comfy-Ui so I might look into this

comments.author: ThaBombs
comments.body:
Depending on what exactly you want to achieve ChatGPT can get you there.

With some tinkering you can get chatgpt to save and use a specific style, though I wouldn't ask it for transparent options. Ask for a single color background that you'd then remove with other tools. There is a very good AI just for that, bgbye. 

It's what I'm using for my 2d assets. Doesn't do animations / spritesheets well though

comments.author: NormandFutz
comments.body: yea what do you need or want

replies.author: rapkannibale
replies.body: Mostly simple 2D or pixel art sprites in a consistent style.

replies.author: NormandFutz
replies.body: Id do it in steps, make the characters by fine tuning your art style and theme so everyone you make is uniform or thematically correct, find a Lora or train one that matches your style, generate the characters in batch until you find a good start or inspiration, fix what you dont like in gimp, zoom the fuck in, its pixelsots not too hard to just fix things so you like it or  maybe re generated via in paint to change colors or fine tune clothing, once the characters are made, with good references it should be easier to make sprites of them is what id do. You can set the size of the image in comfy ui and there are plenty of transparency batching solutions also depending on what way your worlflows are. That's what I did at least but  swapped to 3d models for the combat and didnt go with the sprite route. ​

comments.author: CorySimmons
comments.body:
I made this. [https://spritewash.com](https://spritewash.com)  
  
1. Copy/paste an AI spritesheet to it (generate it with a "solid bright magenta bg")  
2. Eyedropper + threshold to get rid of bg  
3. Double click to extract a sprite  
4. Double click to add the sprite to an animation  
5. Export

This is the fastest/cleanest workflow I've seen and I've tested a lot of them.

Free forever. Syncs your projects with your browser if you're logged out. If you don't want to risk losing them when you flush browser cache, make an account and it'll save them to a remote db. Resizes your raw sprite to your preferred dimensions and resamples with your choice of algo so you don't get mixels (https://www.youtube.com/shorts/OQzApE2FXmI).
